properties.decision:
Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal — the older cement idea (dec:idea-a-design-cements-from-the-core-outward-and-past-a-point-starting-over-is-cheaper-than-unwinding) grown into a measurement. Anthony, 2026-09-06, in his words: "a design 'cemented' measurement could probably be done by seeing how many nodes you would have to go back into a design... like if you had to unpeel seven layers of design decisions to change something, that would be a difficult to alter. hence, you could start measuring both how hard it would be to change a given design and secondly, how cemented is your design. both would be good things to know when a person wants to alter a design. this touches upon a really old brainstorm of having alternate designs or marking decision points in a design."

THE INSTRUMENT, as he states it: for a node X, the decisions it rests on (GOVERNED_BY), the decisions THOSE rest on (Decision→Decision GOVERNED_BY / DEPENDS_ON, and the reverse of EVOLVES_INTO / SUPERSEDES / OBSOLETES), and so on — the length of the longest such chain is the number of layers a change to X must unpeel. Per node it answers "how hard is this to alter"; the distribution over the design answers "how cemented is the design"; the two are the same computation read at two grains.

⭐ WHAT IT READS TODAY, COMPUTED ON THE EXPORT (2026-09-06): of 2,864 design nodes, 228 are governed by any decision at all. Layers to unpeel: 192 nodes at 1, 26 at 2, 6 at 3, 2 at 4, 2 at 5 (cap:brainstorm and cap:an-unconnected-idea-is-visible-as-one are the deepest). Over the 193 accepted Decisions on the design graph, 157 rest on NO other decision; the longest chain is 4. Decision→Decision edges of all kinds: DEPENDS_ON 64, GOVERNED_BY 37, CONTRADICTS 27, ANTICIPATES 23, EVOLVES_INTO 17, OBSOLETES 12, CAUSES 7, BLOCKS 6, MITIGATES 5, RISKS 1. So the instrument, built today, would say reflow2 is barely cemented at all — and that is FALSE, by Anthony's own account and by the sibling measurement (the k=5 core is the schema and the core modules, which everything realizes). The chain he feels when he tries to reverse something runs through PROSE: "distinct from X, which decided Y", "settled by dec:Z" — 632 Decisions and 37 GOVERNED_BY edges between them.

THE FRAMINGS:
(a) BUILD THE INSTRUMENT AS STATED — a `reversal_cost` (per node) and `cement_report` (design-wide distribution) over the recorded decision edges. Cheap: the traversal above is one function; the schema already holds every edge type it needs. Counter-argument: on this design it reads 1 layer for 84% of governed nodes and 0 for 92% of the design, so it would report a soft design and be believed — the wallpaper failure in reverse, a green that measures absence of data rather than absence of cement.
(b) FEED IT FIRST — draw the decision dependencies the prose already states. add_decision's `related_to` exists but the brainstorm skill's linking discipline fires only on `kind: exploratory` and stays off the choice path; a CHOICE decision that says in prose "rests on dec:X" draws nothing. A capture-time step for choice decisions ("which accepted decisions does this one rest on?") is the same one-call shape and would make (a) read true going forward. Counter-argument: backfilling 632 decisions' prose into edges is a session of judgement, and a wrong DEPENDS_ON is a false layer that every later reversal-cost reading repeats.
(c) MEASURE THROUGH REALIZATION INSTEAD OF THROUGH DECISIONS — cost-to-alter X = the size of X's downstream closure over REALIZES / ALLOCATED_TO / SATISFIES / DEPENDS_ON (what propagate_change already walks), not the decision chain. It reads non-zero today (the k-core sibling shows the schema and core modules are exactly the nodes with the largest closures). Counter-argument: it measures blast radius, not unpeeling — how much moves, not how many rulings you must reopen — and Anthony's question was the second one.
(d) DECLARE THE LAYER RATHER THAN COMPUTE IT — a baseline, in his SE vocabulary: an accepted Decision or DesignRule marked as foundation, so the design SAYS what is cemented and a change that touches it is asked "you are reopening a baseline — on whose word?". Counter-argument: declared cement drifts from real cement the same way any status drifts from structure; (a) is what would notice the disagreement.

WHERE THE OLD BRAINSTORM COMES IN: a decision point (cap:decision-point, register_alternative + collapse_decision) is exactly a marked place where a design could have gone another way, and dec:parallel-alternatives settled that alternatives are branch-by-file. Reversal cost is the price of walking back TO a decision point; a design that marked its decision points as it went would have the chain (b) wants, drawn at the moment it was cheapest — which is the argument for (b) over backfilling.
properties.name: OPEN — is "how cemented" measured as the number of decision layers a change must unpeel — per node (how hard is THIS to alter) and design-wide (how cemented is the design) — and what would that instrument read today?
properties.rationale: A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION. The instrument Anthony describes is one traversal and is right in shape; the finding is that it has nothing to traverse yet — 157 of 193 accepted decisions rest on no recorded decision, so built today it would report a soft design and be believed. That puts (b) before (a): the cheapest honest move is a capture-time question on CHOICE decisions ("which accepted decisions does this rest on?"), the same one-call shape the brainstorm skill already uses for ideas, so the chain is drawn when it is cheapest and the measurement reads true going forward rather than after a backfill nobody will do. (c) is available today and answers the neighbouring question (blast radius); (d) is his own vocabulary and would make "we are past the point of overhaul" a statement the design carries rather than a feeling. This is the third brainstorm in one evening to land on the same missing edge — decision-to-decision structure lives in prose — from convergence, from reversibility and now from measurement, which is itself evidence that the edge is the thing to build if any of this is. Nothing here is proposed; Anthony's call whether (b) earns a session.
